reason: The text describes the Israelites suffering under Egyptian slavery and crying out in distress (וַיִּזְעָ֑קוּ - they cried out to God from their labor). However, there is no evidence that they blame their leaders or Yahweh for putting them at risk. Instead, the passage portrays: (1) God responding compassionately to their cries by hearing them and remembering his covenant, (2) God commanding Moses to deliver them, and (3) the Israelites' failure to listen to Moses stemming from their despair and hardship (מִקֹּ֣צֶר ר֔וּחַ וּמֵעֲבֹדָ֖ה קָשָֽׁה - shortness of spirit and hard labor), not from blame toward their leaders. The text presents the Israelites as victims of Egyptian oppression being rescued by Yahweh, not as people blaming their leaders or deity for their plight.
